newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians demonstrate against Jerusalem tunnel.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians demonstrate against Jerusalem tunnel.

text.p: Hundreds of Palestinians demonstrated in Jerusalem's Old City on Tuesday against the opening by Israel of a tunnel near the Temple Mount, site of Islam's third holiest shrine, witnesses said.

Workmen completed the tunnel overnight, working under heavy guard. Israel hailed it as an important archaeological site. But Palestinians complained it would upset the religious status quo in Jerusalem.

In Jabalya camp, Gaza Strip, Palestinian President Yasser Arafat told policemen: "This is a crime, a big crime against our religious and holy places." He called it a breach of Israeli-PLO peace deals.
Palestinian merchants closed shops in protest. There were no immediate reports of stone-throwing.

The tunnel runs along the Wailing Wall, the retaining wall below the Dome of the Rock and Al-Aqsa mosques. It comes out on the Via Dolorosa, the traditional route travelled by Jesus before his crucifixion.

Deputy Israeli Mayor of Jerusalem Shmuel Meir praised right-wing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for deciding to complete the tunnel while other prime ministers had resisted, apparently for fear of triggering Palestinian violence.
But senior Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat told Reuters: "Such policies push the Palestinians and Israelis towards...confrontation and catastrophe."
